subject: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@sierrahealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@sierracorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a short renewal proposal that tries to balance Sierra's seasonal surge risk with Redwood's capacity planning needs. High level: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal start 2026-07-01)
- Commit: move from current 1.2M tokens/mo to a stepped commit (1.2M months 1-3, 1.6M months 4-12)
- Surge-safeguard: capped overage rate through a "surge carveout" bucket (30% buffer for Q4 spikes)
- One-time retention credit: $25k applied to first invoice if signed by 2026-06-30

We modeled the carveout so it only covers prefix/latency-sensitive traffic (chat/query paths) and excludes experimental batch workloads — that keeps unit economics stable. Ben and Karthik are copied for technical/ops constraints.

Please review the attached draft (Sierra_Renewal_Draft_v2.pdf) and the usage CSV I pulled for Q1 so you can validate the suggested commit ladder. Quick ask: can you confirm whether the Q4 surge is internal forecast-driven or tied to marketing campaigns? That determines whether we gate the carveout to specific services.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Sierra_Renewal_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF - proposal), sierra_q1_usage.csv (CSV - usage export)
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@sierrahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@sierracorp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal

Olga — thanks, appreciate the clear options. A few initial notes: 

- Q4 risk is real but tied to a product launch (new teletriage feature) and a multi-week campaign in Oct-Nov. We expect short spikes rather than sustained elevation.
- The carveout sounds useful but we need assurance on predictability (we can’t have exponential overage charges during the campaign).
- The $25k retention credit is helpful; procurement will still ask for a small cap on annual price movement.

Can Ben weigh in on how you isolate prefix traffic for the carveout? Also looping Tom (ops) to confirm whether we can restrict the carveout to a named service.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jenkins
Head of Platform Operations
Sierra Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@sierrahealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal

Sara — quick technical note: we can gate the carveout to specific API routes or model IDs. Implementation options:

- Route-level carveout: tag teletriage endpoints; only tokens from those routes draw from the surge bucket.
- Token-type carveout: limit to low-latency chat tokens (prefix + short completion).

Operational considerations: carveout tokens are metered separately and priced at the capped overage rate in the draft. If you want strict caps, we can implement an auto-fallback that routes excess traffic to a lower-cost model variant once the carveout is exhausted. That gives predictability at the expense of occasional quality drop.

If helpful, I can spin up an isolation test in a sandbox tomorrow and share a short log export for your SREs.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts 
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@sierracorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@sierrahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal

Ben — that sounds promising. A couple clarifying questions for procurement: 

1) If we use route-level carveout, how will reporting look? We need daily breakdowns for billing reconciliation.
2) Can you confirm the fallback SLA? If traffic moves to a cheaper model during surge, what's the expected latency delta and error profile?

Also, Sara — procurement will want the retention credit documented in the Master Subscription Agreement so it's visible to finance. We may also request a small price-floor guarantee to limit annual increases to <7%.

Tom
IT Ops Lead
Sierra Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@sierracorp.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@sierrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal

Tom / Sara — answered inline: 

1) Reporting: we can provide a daily CSV with per-route token counts and a summarized monthly invoice CSV. We'll also expose the per-route prefix in your dashboard and a webhook you can pull.

2) Fallback SLA: expected latency delta for the cheaper variant is +30-70ms median, p95 +100-150ms depending on sequence length. Error profile: no increased error rate expected; quality drop is task-dependent (we'll mark fallback traffic in logs so you can sample for QA).

Next steps I propose: 
- Sign the attached amendment with the carveout language and the $25k retention credit visible on page 2.
- Redwood to deliver a sandbox isolation test by Wed 2026-06-24.
- Sierra to provide a short list of named routes for the carveout (1-3 endpoints).

Olga / Ben — can you confirm DocuSign link and credit placement? I’ll prepare the operational checklist for the sandbox.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@sierrahealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@sierracorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit carveout & surge-safeguard — renewal pricing proposal

Perfect — I updated the draft to show the $25k retention credit as an invoice line (see p2) and added the carveout definition language we discussed. DocuSign link is the second related link above; I'll send an execution copy tomorrow morning with the sandbox checklist.

If procurement needs a price-floor clause, we can add a 7% annual movement cap to the amendment (finance will need a short review but that is doable).

Next milestone: sign by 2026-06-30 to secure the retention credit and the stepped commit pricing.

Olga
